extra.message: SQL injection: user-controlled req.query['region'] is interpolated directly into the SQL string passed to AppDataSource.query() (`WHERE city ILIKE '%${region}%' OR state ILIKE '%${region}%'`). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the region parameter (e.g. '%' OR 1=1 --). Unlike other queries in this file it is not parameterized.

OS command injection: the attacker-controlled `format` query parameter is neither validated nor allowlisted (compare renderPortfolioSummary which restricts to pdf/html/docx) and is concatenated into a shell command executed by execSync() at line 200 (`pandoc ${draftPath} -o ${outputPath} -t ${outputFormat}`). A value such as `pdf; <cmd>` allows arbitrary command execution as the server process.

Path traversal (arbitrary file write): `noteFileName` comes from the request body and is joined with path.join(COMPLIANCE_STAGING_DIR, noteFileName) without any basename/sanitization, then written with fs.writeFileSync(). A fileName of `../../app.js` (or similar) lets an authenticated underwriter/support user write attacker-controlled content to any path the process can write, potentially leading to code execution. The sibling archiveReviewMemo handler correctly uses path.basename().

Path traversal (arbitrary file write): `fileName` in the request body is joined with path.join(PRODUCT_ASSETS_DIR, fileName) and written with fs.writeFileSync() with no basename/allowlist check. An admin can write files outside the assets directory (e.g. fileName='../../dist/index.js') to overwrite application files, enabling code execution on restart.

Path traversal (arbitrary file read): `profile.letterheadFilename` is borrower-controlled (PUT /api/borrowers/my allows setting letterheadFilename) and is used as fs.readFileSync(path.join(LETTERHEAD_DIR, filename)). There is no containment check such as the one applied in previewBusinessSignature (startsWith baseDir), so a stored value like '../.env' or '../src/data-source.ts' lets a borrower read arbitrary server files when a staff member previews the letterhead.

Server-Side Request Forgery: importDocumentTemplateContent fetches the caller-supplied `x-template-source-url` header with no host allowlist (contrast previewExternalTemplateSource which restricts to templates.lendingco-partners.com). An admin can make the server fetch arbitrary internal/cloud-metadata URLs and return the response body.

Open redirect: /api/auth/continue redirects (res.redirect) to `nextUrl` built from the attacker-controllable `x-redirect-url` header (or Referer) with no allowlist. An attacker can point the redirect to an external site, enabling phishing / credential-harvesting redirects.

IDOR / missing object-level authorization: PUT /api/payment-accounts/:id/designate-primary loads any PaymentAccount by id with no ownership or role check (any authenticated borrower can target any account). The caller can flip another business's primary payout account and overwrite its bankName/routingNumber, tampering with disbursement payout data for a loan that does not belong to them.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Broken authentication / authorization on partner endpoints: /api/payment-accounts/partner-status is completely unauthenticated and grants access purely on the client-supplied `x-partner-role == 'ledger-service'` header (line 341). Any caller can set this header to bypass the intended gateway restriction. The ledger-sync endpoints (/ledger-sync, /ledger-sync/start at lines 200/227) are likewise unauthenticated and rely on a JWT signed with LEDGER_SYNC_SECRET that falls back to a hardcoded default ('ledger-sync-partner-secret-dev-only', line 13); /ledger-sync/start mints a valid session token for any known accountId, and resumeLedgerSyncSession verifies with ignoreExpiration:true.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: LDAP injection: findEmployeeByBadgeId builds the LDAP filter `(uid=${badgeId})` by interpolating the raw `badge_id` query parameter without escaping. Contrast verifyComplianceGroupMembership which sanitizes via ldapEscape(). A value such as `*` expands the filter to match every directory entry, disclosing the whole staff directory.

Broken authentication + user enumeration: the partner-referral endpoints authenticate the caller only by the presence of a cookie named partner_session whose value is never validated or signed, and no code path ever issues that cookie. Anyone can send partner_session=anything and access checkReferralEligibility, which then reveals whether a given email is registered (404 vs eligible:true) - an unauthenticated email-enumeration oracle.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Hardcoded default password: every borrower lead imported via the CSV endpoint is created with the same known password 'Welcome123!' (admin.ts POST /users line 58 also defaults to it). Since these accounts are real businesses, an attacker can sign in as any imported lead before the lead does, gaining full account control.

Hardcoded fallback JWT signing secret: JWT_SECRET defaults to the well-known value 'loan-origination-jwt-secret-dev-only'. If JWT_SECRET is not set in the environment, anyone knowing this default can forge valid authentication tokens (id/email/role) and impersonate any user, including admin, bypassing authentication entirely.

Sensitive data exposure: on failure, preparePayoutDraft logs the entire request body (console.error), which contains the borrower's bankName, routingNumber and accountNumberLast4. Plaintext banking details are written to application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
